- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ days), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch mean reversion.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and use sentiment momentum as trigger.
